extracted.intended_audience: general moviegoers, film fans, and readers interested in Roger Ebert's curated film selections
extracted.subtask_description: An editorial Rotten Tomatoes page that reproduces and celebrates Roger Ebert's curated list of 'Great Movies', showing each film's Tomatometer, a short critics' consensus, synopsis, cast and director. The page is an alphabetical, paginated compilation intended for discovery and reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roger Ebert's 'Great Movies' selection (4-star/thumbs-up)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Before he passed away in 2013, he tactfully amassed a list of over 350 4-star/thumbs-up films that he called Great Movies."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the primary inclusion criterion for the list: films Ebert rated as four stars/thumbs-up and labeled 'Great Movies' by him. The page reproduces/displays those selections to celebrate his life and work; readers are directed to view Ebert’s full Great Movies list via a link. (Editorial note on the page: the list is being presented alphabetically for discovery.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Tomatometer percentage (critic aggregation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each film entry displays a percentage (e.g., "100%", "90%", "68%"), indicating the film's Tomatometer score as shown on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The percentage is Rotten Tomatoes' aggregated critics' score presented next to each film. On this page it is used as an at-a-glance quantitative indicator of critical reception; some entries show a dash or 'No consensus yet' when consensus/aggregation data is unavailable or insufficient. The page does not detail Tomatometer methodology here, but consistently displays the score per film.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critics Consensus (short qualitative summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry includes a "Critics Consensus:" line followed by a brief evaluative sentence or phrase (for example, "A seminal French New Wave film that offers an honest, sympathetic, and wholly heartbreaking observation of adolescence without trite nostalgia.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These short synoptic statements summarize the overall critical view of the film and accompany the Tomatometer. They serve as concise qualitative judgments—sometimes marked explicitly as 'No consensus yet' when a consensus summary hasn't been composed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopsis / Starring / Directed By metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: For every film listed the page provides a short synopsis, a 'Starring:' list, and a 'Directed By:' credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not evaluative scoring criteria, these consistent metadata fields contextualize each film for readers and support discovery and assessment (e.g., helping readers judge interest based on plot, cast, or director). Each synopsis is brief with a 'View Full Synopsis' link for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical listing / editorial ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: "To celebrate his life and the films he championed (seriously, they’re all amazing), we’re listing them all in alphabetical order for everyone to discover."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page's organization is an explicit editorial choice: the Great Movies selections are presented alphabetically (paginated) rather than by ranking, Tomatometer, or date. This affects discoverability and implies neutrality regarding internal ranking among Ebert's picks.
